changes.title: Enact reciprocal tariff authority so the US can match partners' tariffs and barriers

summary: Four official documents that could not be opened on their hosts in earlier reviews were retrieved from the official hosts, or from the Internet Archive snapshot of the official address for the first, supplied to the project, and read against their text layers: the Secretary of War memorandum of 2025-11-07 redesignating the Defense Acquisition System as the Warfighting Acquisition System (43 pages); the DHS FY2027 congressional budget justification for CISA (279 pages); the final report of the President's Council to Assess FEMA dated 2026-05-07 (75 pages); and the presidential proclamation of 2026-10-23 further modifying the scope of the Section 338 duties on Canadian products, with its two annexes. Two independent reviewers rewrote the four records from the documents in place of the law-firm, trade-press and CRS accounts they had relied on. c04-04 rose from 70 to 82 and c05-08 from 63 to 80 (the stage-deciding document was read on the official host), c05-09 from 62 to 72 (the proposal is now read, but the operative cuts still rest on news and a state official's letter, and the justification never uses the word misinformation), c26-01 stayed at 72 with two events added. No stage or progress changed. The three leads that had waited since 2026-10-11 on these hosts are closed.
title: Blocked official documents retrieved and read, 2026-10-26
